questions.answer:
The principal range of arcsine is \([-\pi/2,\pi/2]\). In that interval, the angle with sine \(-\sqrt3/2\) is
\[
-\frac{\pi}{3}
\]
Therefore
\[
\arcsin(-\sqrt3/2)=-\frac{\pi}{3}
\]

The principal range of arccosine is \([0,\pi]\). The angle in that interval with cosine \(0\) is
\[
\frac{\pi}{2}
\]
so \(\arccos(0)=\pi/2\).

The principal range of arctangent is \((-\pi/2,\pi/2)\). The angle in that interval with tangent \(-1\) is
\[
-\frac{\pi}{4}
\]

The principal angle is \(\arcsin(1/2)=\pi/6\). Sine is positive in quadrants I and II, so within one full turn
\[
\theta=\frac{\pi}{6},\qquad \theta=\pi-\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{5\pi}{6}
\]

The principal arccosine value is \(3\pi/4\). Cosine has the same value at the symmetric angle \(-3\pi/4\), then repeats every \(2\pi\). Hence
\[
\theta=\pm\frac{3\pi}{4}+2\pi k,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z
\]

questions.prompt: A vector has components \(x=-3\) and \(y=4\). Why is \(\arctan(y/x)\) alone not enough to identify its direction from the positive \(x\)-axis?
questions.answer:
Here
\[
\frac{y}{x}=\frac{4}{-3}=-\frac43
\]
The value \(\arctan(-4/3)\) lies in the principal arctangent range, which is quadrant IV. But the vector \((-3,4)\) is in quadrant II. The ratio gives the tangent, but the signs of both components are needed to choose the correct quadrant.
